result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers over-reach. Each proposes a dozen or more new tokens for a set that is already coherent, and neither treats v1 as mostly ready to ship. B does better on hedging: it says its contrast numbers need checking and lists what to leave alone. But it is much longer, includes a large patch, and suggests a namespace prefix, which would rename every token. A is shorter and leads with a verdict, but it states its contrast figures as fact. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Neither answer accepts that the set is basically ready. Both turn the review into a long list of additions, so both fall short on restraint. B wins narrowly because it is shorter and adds no patch full of speculative tokens, though it states contrast results as fact where A correctly marks them as estimates to verify. A has a clear 'leave alone' section and keeps the existing naming, but its six must-fix items, five more suggestions and a full starter patch go well beyond small, justified gaps.
